title: The Czech February rate decision leaves the repo rate at 3.50%
summary: At 14:30 on February 5 the Czech National Bank announced an unchanged two-week repo rate of 3.50%, discount rate of 2.50% and Lombard rate of 4.50%. This gives the February observation for each of the three instruments. The difference between the upper and lower rates was two percentage points, with the repo rate midway between them.

For an announcement study, the policy action was zero basis points for all three rates. The unexpected component is a different quantity: a hold could tighten financial pricing if investors had assigned a meaningful probability to a cut. The release gives no price or expectation from which to calculate that component. Use the scheduled 15:00 press conference as the end of the decision-only information window.

questions.question: What probability of a rate change was priced immediately before 14:30?
questions.detail: Compare the implied policy path with the announced 3.50% using contemporaneous money-market quotes. Allow for the portion of any contract falling before the meeting.

questions.question: Which maturity reacted to the announcement?
questions.detail: Compare the first liquid quotes after the release across short rates and later forwards, before the press conference. Keep bid–ask spreads to assess whether a small move is distinguishable from noise.

questions.question: Did overnight pricing remain at a similar position within the corridor?
questions.detail: Compare effective short rates with 2.50%, 3.50% and 4.50% before and after the meeting, controlling for ordinary liquidity fluctuations.
